CNBC 23 Nov

U.S. Treasury yields rose on Monday, partially unwinding price action seen at the end of last week, as stocks experienced a strong rebound on Wall Street and investors looked ahead to comments from John Williams of the New York Fed.

The 10-year Treasury yield — the key benchmark for mortgages, student loans and credit card debt — was up 4 basis points to 4.952%.

The 2-year Treasury note yield, the most sensitive to short-term Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, was up more than 10 basis points at 4.719%. The 30-year Treasury bond yield — which often reacts the most to geopolitical developments — was up 15 basis points to 5.317%.

One basis point equals 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.

"Assets that had offered a measure of safety last week have retreated today," said Thierry Wizman, global FX and rates strategist at Macquarie Group. "If stocks have ended their slide, as today's action seems to suggest, the Fed is likelier to follow-through with a 25bp rate hike on December 9, even while the 50bp hike now feels like an impossibility."

Recent economic data and hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve policymakers have reinforced market expectations for further interest rate hikes. Traders are pricing in a roughly 98% chance of a quarter-percentage-point rise in the fed funds rate in December, up from around 88% on Friday, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Williams is due to speak later on Monday and could offer insights on the outlook for the economy and monetary policy.

Revised GDP data due on Wednesday is expected to confirm that the U.S. economy expanded by 3.4% in the third quarter, according to Trading Economics forecasts. This compares to 2.2% growth in the second quarter.

The October reading of the personal consumption expenditures price index, which measures underlying inflation, is also due Wednesday. A rise of 0.3% is expected, according to economists polled by Dow Jones.

September's PCE reading showed an increase of 0.5% for the month, which put the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. That marked the largest monthly gain since March.
